chip.label: Timeline
chip.title: A timeline for DaVinci Resolve, Premiere Pro or Final Cut Pro, with chapter markers
editor.resolve.label: DaVinci Resolve
editor.resolve.title: Writes an FCPXML file. In Resolve: File › Import › Timeline…
editor.premiere.label: Premiere Pro
editor.premiere.title: Writes a Premiere XML file. In Premiere: File › Import…
editor.finalcut.label: Final Cut Pro
editor.finalcut.title: Writes an FCPXML file for a Mac. Made on Windows: keep the files together and, on the Mac, use File › Relink Files…
editor.edl.label: Other editor (EDL)
editor.edl.title: A CMX 3600 EDL with the finished video, for editors that read EDL
uses.export.label: This export
uses.export.hint: The finished video and its sound, with chapter markers. Looks the same in every editor.
uses.recordings.label: The original recordings
uses.recordings.hint: Your cuts, speed changes and pauses over the original screen, camera and sound. Zooms, cursor effects, the background, captions, texts and the camera layout are not carried, and the camera is on track 2, turned off. The recordings are copied next to the timeline.
uses.premierePitch: Speed changes may change the pitch in Premiere Pro.
blocked.finalcutCodec: Final Cut Pro cannot open {codec} files. Choose H.264 or HEVC.
blocked.edlRecordings: An EDL can hold the finished video only. Choose This export.
unchecked: Not checked yet with {editor}: it may not open {codec} files.
done.resolve: In DaVinci Resolve: File › Import › Timeline…
done.finalcut: In Final Cut Pro: File › Import › XML…, then File › Relink Files… for the media
done.edl: In your editor: import the EDL and link it to {video}
done.markers: In DaVinci Resolve: right-click the timeline in the Media Pool, then Timelines › Import › Timeline Markers from EDL…
done.failed: The timeline could not be saved: {reason}
